guidance.summary: Cleveland-Cliffs expects Q4 2026 adjusted EBITDA of approximately $715 million and a major Q4 debt reduction, says it remains on track for leverage under 2.5x net debt to EBITDA by mid-2027, and expects 2027 adjusted EBITDA to exceed $4 billion.

guidance.sentence: We expect fourth quarter adjusted EBITDA to further increase, even with typical fourth-quarter seasonality and planned maintenance outages.
We continued to reduce debt in Q3 and, with amplified free cash flow in Q4 and property sale proceeds, we expect a major debt reduction in the fourth quarter.
With all that, we remain on track to reach our leverage target of under 2.5x net debt to EBITDA by the middle of next year.
Based on the new contracts we have already signed with our clients and prevailing index price forecasts, we would expect our 2027 adjusted EBITDA to exceed $4 billion.

The Company expects fourth-quarter 2026 adjusted EBITDA 2 to be approximately $715 million, an increase from the third quarter as a result of increased pricing, partially offset by seasonality, increased maintenance outages, input costs and incentive compensation accruals.
Based on 2027 contract changes and prevailing price forecasts, the Company would expect 2027 adjusted EBITDA to exceed $4 billion.

writeup.headline: Cleveland-Cliffs rates Sell as weak margins and a stretched balance sheet outweigh improving growth and momentum.
writeup.thesis: Cleveland-Cliffs scores 41, a Sell, held down mainly by quality (10) and balance sheet (0). Gross margin is 1.5%, operating margin -1.4% and FCF margin -2.4%, with the diluted share count up 16.0% year on year, and cash covers only 0.01 of debt while free cash flow is negative. Valuation scores 19: P/S of 0.4 is low in absolute terms, but negative FCF and EBIT leave no P/FCF or EV/EBIT, and the FCF yield is 11.1 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield; against its own history, P/S is more expensive than at 42 of the last 61 month-ends, while P/FCF is not comparable (negative now and in 21 of 61 month-ends) and EV/EBIT is not comparable (negative now and in 24 of 61 month-ends). Offsetting this, growth scores 72 on latest-quarter revenue growth of 18.6% year on year, with growth that sped up by 12.6 pp from the previous quarter, and trend scores 72 with the price 22.6% above its 200-day average. News is mildly positive (64): management guided Q4 2026 adjusted EBITDA to about $715 million, expects 2027 adjusted EBITDA to exceed $4 billion and targets leverage under 2.5x by mid-2027.
key_risks: Very thin margins and negative free cash flow leave little cushion if steel prices or volumes soften
Heavy debt with almost no cash relative to it; the deleveraging plan depends on hitting EBITDA targets
Diluted share count up 16.0% year on year, diluting existing holders
Canadian government threat of court action over Stelco layoffs under Investment Canada Act commitments
Tariff-linked weak demand has led Stelco to idle Hamilton cold-rolled and coated lines
what_would_change: A 4-point rise in the score would lift the rating to Hold, for example from margins or free cash flow turning positive and improving the quality and valuation scores
Delivering the promised Q4 debt reduction and progress toward leverage under 2.5x would help the balance sheet score from its current 0
A 12-point drop would push it to Strong Sell, for instance if growth or the share-price trend reversed or guidance were cut
An escalation of the Stelco dispute into court action could weigh further on the news score
